newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline slips gains but arbitrage supportive.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline slips gains but arbitrage supportive.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices slipped from early gains as NYMEX unleaded gave back some of Wednesday's one cent a gallon gain, but traders said the "almost open" arbitrage and cheaper freight costs were supportive.
"The opening arb may mean that the NWE market is not as long as many people think it is," one trader said.
She said the combination of NYMEX gains and cheaper freight cost were beginning to make arbitrage look more attractive.
Arbitrage cargoes were on offer at around August NYMEX -5 cents a gallon with freight costs for 30kt slipping from worldscale 200-220 to worldscale 170 in the past week.
NWE cargoes prices for Eurograde stood around $1 firmer at $187/$189 a tonne late trade.

Barges were slightly easier. Following trade as high as $187 in the morning for prompt lifting refinery Rotterdam eurograde barges the general ARA market was traded and valued around $182 in late business off 50 cents to $1 on the day.
The market slipped between contango and backwardation during the day but ended with a $1-2 backwardation reflecting the opening arbitrage to the U.S.
